full_judgment:
20. It is conveniently observed that, though sad, yet it is a fact that in out country there is a tendency on the part of the people to rope in as many people as possible for facing trial in respect of death of any victim. It has been found that innocent persons including aged, infirm, rivals including political rivals are booked for standing on the dock. Some are acquitted by Court of first instance and some by Appellate Court but only after having been in incarceration for years. Such efforts on the part of relatives of the victim and other interested persons invariably but unfortunately, help the real culprit or culprits as it becomes difficult on the part of Court/Tribunal to shift grain out of chaff. Under such circumstances and in view of prevalent Criminal Jurisprudential System, the Doctrine of Presumption of Innocence in favour of the accused makes justice system a victim which ultimately, weakens the Criminal Justice Dispensation System. 

 49. A duty is cast upon prosecution to explore every avenue open to it to unveil truth and bring to book the real offenders and to advance cause of justice. Witnesses who can throw sufficient light in unfolding truth are to be produced in the witness box as prosecution witnesses. Non-examination of material witnesses shall give rise to a strong presumption against prosecution case in respect of involvement of an accused in the felony allegedly committed by him. If a material witness who would unroll the genesis of incident is not convincingly brought to fore otherwise or where there is a gap or infirmity in the prosecution case which could have been supplied or provided by examining a witness who, though, available is not examined, prosecution case can be termed as suffering from a serious deficiency and infirmity and with-holding of such a material and vital witness would oblige the Court to draw an adverse inference against the prosecution by holding that if the witness would have been examined he would not have supported the prosecution case as projected. 

 53. The inevitable legal presumption which flows is that the persons stated above, if would have been examined, would not have definitely supported the prosecution case in abridgement of convict-appellant in causing the homicidal death of deceased Michael. On this score, also, convict-appellant is entitled to get the benefit of doubt.
